Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3358; immoderate:--(thing) without measure.
BiblicalUsage: Without measure, immoderate, and Paul uses it twice to say what he will not do. We will not boast of things without our measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God hath distributed to us. And again, not boasting of things without our measure, that is, of other men's labours; the word is the boast that goes past the boundary God set.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for without measure carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the boundary, that Paul will boast only inside the measure God gave him and not in another man's work.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
